answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring each new agent to lock scarce collateral and pass randomly assigned cross-agent tasks before earning payment. Existing agents accept it only after a bridge audit checks behavior across domains; knoll and saffron challenge sets expose copied or coordinated models, and inconsistent answers trigger quorum review and slashing. A Sybil attacker must fund every persona, wait for reputation, and risk losing deposits, making mass identities costlier than the fraud they enable.
